subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what exact trigger plus local editor/tempfile safety contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation shape is clear, but the feature launches an environment-selected local process and writes prompt drafts to disk, and the current shortcut/keybinding surface has a conflict that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve guarded core TUI flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an explicit maintainer-approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe $VISUAL/$EDITOR handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Keep open pending UX decision
options.body: Leave the issue open until maintainers choose the shortcut or slash-command model and decide whether this should reuse or replace the inactive app.editor.external keybinding entry.

options.title: Decline external process handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers decide inline multiline editing and composer expansion are the preferred long-prompt solutions instead of launching local editors from the TUI.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded core TUI flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an explicit maintainer-approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe $VISUAL/$EDITOR handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact request and recently changed the same TUI command surface, making him the best available product/security routing owner from the observed history.
